title: The Deer With Human Teeth
hook: At the edge of the city, a deer steps from a shelterbelt and smiles with the missing teeth of people who vanished from a rural bus stop.
truth: The animal is a mask worn by a famine spirit that trades hunger for obedience and leaves human marks in animal mouths.

monster.name: The White-Browed Hart
monster.instinct: To make hungry people bargain away their names, teeth, and choices.
weaknesses: bread shared freely at a crossroads
calling each taken person's full name before dawn

countdown.label: First Sign
countdown.text: A deer watches traffic from the ditch and smiles with a child's missing front tooth.

countdown.label: First Loss
countdown.text: A commuter disappears, leaving lunch untouched and steaming in the shelter.

countdown.label: Spread
countdown.text: People nearby dream of chewing snow and wake with sore gums.

countdown.label: Bargain
countdown.text: The Hart offers food, warmth, and safety in exchange for a name.

countdown.label: Crisis
countdown.text: A silent herd surrounds the bus loop and every animal has one human tooth.

countdown.label: Finale
countdown.text: The shelterbelt opens into a white winter road where the taken walk without names.

clues.text: Dental records match teeth found in the mouths of living deer.
Animals refuse bread left alone but bow when it is shared among strangers.
A gate latch burns a pale mark into velvet shed from an antler.
The missing are remembered by faces and habits, but their names slide away.
Untouched lunches at the bus stop are all missing bread.
A thin line of snow cuts through the shelterbelt despite warm weather.

keeperHints: Make the rural edge feel close to the city, not distant wilderness.
The Hart should be polite, patient, and visibly hungry.
Use teeth and names sparingly so each appearance lands.
revealPolicy: Reveal the bargain economy before revealing the Hart's full road into winter.
automationSafety: Do not remove a player character's name or body part without explicit permission.
Offer bargains clearly as choices, with costs visible enough to matter.
